baseProblem.statement: Given an array of non-negative integers representing heights of vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum area.

rounds.question: What initial state powers the two-pointer sweep?

options.conceptLabel: Pointers at both ends, best area zero

fragments.java: int lo = 0, hi = height.length - 1; int best = 0;

options.rationale: The widest container is the full span; start there, shrink inward, and track the best area seen.

options.conceptLabel: One pointer and a running sum
options.rationale: Area depends on a PAIR of lines; one pointer and a sum can't express the width-times-height relationship.
Sorting destroys positions, but width is the distance between original indices — you'd measure lines that aren't really that far apart.

options.conceptLabel: Pointers at both ends, best seeded with a height

fragments.java: int lo = 0, hi = height.length - 1; int best = height[0];

options.rationale: Seeding best with a height (not an area) can mis-count; the correct starting best is 0.

options.conceptLabel: Once per index, left to right
options.rationale: A single moving index gives no opposing wall; the area needs two converging pointers, not one sweep.

options.conceptLabel: While the two pointers have not met
options.rationale: Each step discards the shorter wall and narrows the window, finishing in one linear pass.

fragments.python:
for i in range(len(height)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(height)):
fragments.java: for (int i = 0; i < height.length; i++) for (int j = i + 1; j < height.length; j++) {

options.rationale: Checking every pair is O(n^2); the two-pointer insight reaches the same answer in O(n).

options.conceptLabel: While lo is less than or equal to hi
options.rationale: When lo == hi the width is zero — a pointless iteration that signals an off-by-one.

rounds.question: How do you compute this pair's area?

options.conceptLabel: Sum of the heights times the width
options.rationale: Water is capped by the SHORTER wall; summing overstates capacity past where it would spill over.
The taller wall holds no water above the shorter one; use the min, not the max.
The container holds water up to the lower of the two walls, across the distance between them.

options.conceptLabel: Shorter wall times the left index
options.rationale: Width is the DISTANCE between the lines (hi - lo), not a single index.

rounds.question: After scoring, which pointer should move?

options.rationale: Blindly advancing lo can step past a tall left wall that pairs well later; you must move the shorter side.

options.conceptLabel: Record the best, then drop the shorter wall

fragments.java:
best = Math.max(best, area);
            if (height[lo] < height[hi]) lo++; else hi--;

options.rationale: The shorter wall caps this and every narrower window with it, so discarding it is the only move that can improve the area.

fragments.java:
best = Math.max(best, area);
            if (height[lo] < height[hi]) hi--; else lo++;

options.rationale: Discarding the taller wall keeps the limiting short wall while throwing away height — exactly backwards.
Collapsing both at once skips candidate pairs and can miss the optimal container.
best holds the maximum over every window considered — the answer.
The final window is the narrowest, rarely the best; you need the running maximum.
When the loop ends the pointers have met, so this is 0 — and width isn't the area anyway.
The answer is an area (height times width), not a single height.
